questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more likely to be slippery.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. The vehicle could back up, or you may need to move out of the way of a vehicle coming up behind you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle and car crashes are caused by the driver failing to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger in the vehicle may tell the driver that you are there.
Is illegal because you have to ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center portion of the lane where the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve safely, apply light pressure to the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: The center portion of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect.
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect.
questions.explanation: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect in the center of a lane. Utility hole covers and other hazards can also be found there.

questions.question: Which of the following may be a rectangular sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are usually rectangular with white background and black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue while riding?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue while riding, wear clothing that protects you from wind and rain. Do not ride more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may feel extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, push lightly on the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, push the left grip, then push the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, slow down and shift to a lower gear as you approach it. Then accelerate and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best and no lane position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position based on the current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a tight group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to be split up.
The riders will reach their destination faster in a tight group than in a spread out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: The riders will reach their destination faster in a tight group than in a spread out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than riding spread out because the group uses less road space, is easier for others to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights or during passes.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders who wear helmets are three times more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets. This is true regardless of speed.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best and no lane position should always be avoided. Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change. Pick a position that gives you the most space and makes you easier for other drivers to see.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially deadly ones. Studies show that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Not use any brakes, but downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you brake with maximum stopping power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum braking power comes from using the front and rear brakes together at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When you are in a dangerous area, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This way you can react faster to hazards.

questions.question: Who should control the speed when riding in a group?
questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the speed for the group. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: What may you need to adjust to carry a passenger?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks to handle this weight. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: What should you remember when going through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Always stay on the left side of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Always stay on the right side of the lane throughout the entire curve.
The best path through a curve may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path through a curve may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions can change. Be ready to change your position in the lane when needed. The safest path through a curve may not match the curve of the road.
